newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Japan economist warns of dlr weakness.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Japan economist warns of dlr weakness.

text.p: The fundamentals of the dollar remain weak as the United States continues to post a huge deficit in international investment, Kenji Mizutani, president of Tokai Research and Consulting Inc, said in an interview on Friday.
Mizutani is well-known in Japan for predicting the fall of the dollar below 90 yen last spring, in which the greenback ultimately hit a post-war global low of 79.75 yen in mid-April.
He said the current strength of the dollar was a reflection of the strong U.S. economy and mirrored the trust that investors had in the dollar.
But he said the greenback was actually standing on unstable ground and added that investors were not aware of this.

"Overseas investors are lending money to the United States by holding large amounts of dollar (assets). But they're lending more money to someone who's already heavily loaded with debt," Mizutani said, explaining how the United States ran an international investment deficit of $814 billion in 1995.
The deficit is the difference between foreigners' holdings in the United States and Americans' holdings abroad.
"If everyone says they want their money back, the U.S. won't be able to pay them," he said.
Mizutani said the catalyst for a downward spiral of the dollar could come from the U.S. government itself.

He said the Clinton administration may choose to lower the value of the dollar in order to slash its trade deficit, and the move could trigger a sell-off of dollars from investors fearing further losses in their dollar assets.
"Once people start selling their dollars, there's no end as there's so many people holding dollar (assets)," he added.
